title: The 5 Highest Bridges on Earth, Ranked (All Five Are in One Country)

scenes.text: The five highest bridges on Earth. All five were built by the same country.

scenes.label: Jin'an Bridge · 461 m
scenes.text: Number five: the Jin'an Bridge in Yunnan, China. Its deck hangs 461 meters above the Jinsha River.

scenes.label: Puli Bridge · 485 m
scenes.text: Number four: the Puli Bridge, also in Yunnan. 485 meters of air under the road, open since 2015.

scenes.label: Sidu River Bridge · 496 m
scenes.text: Number three: the Sidu River Bridge in Hubei. 496 meters. It opened in 2009.

scenes.label: Duge Bridge · 565 m
scenes.text: Number two: the Duge Bridge, 565 meters above the Beipan River. It was the highest on Earth from 2016.

scenes.label: Huajiang Canyon Bridge · 625 m
scenes.text: Number one: the Huajiang Canyon Bridge in Guizhou, opened in 2025. 625 meters up, over the same river. A two-hour detour now takes two minutes.

description:
The five highest bridges on Earth, ranked by how far the deck is above the ground or water below.
All five are in China. The Huajiang Canyon Bridge in Guizhou opened in 2025 with its deck 625 metres above the Beipan River, taking the record from the Duge Bridge (565 m, 2016) over the same river. Then come the Sidu River Bridge (496 m, 2009), the Puli Bridge (485 m, 2015) and the Jin'an Bridge (461 m, 2020).
Would you drive across number one?
first_comment: The highest bridge outside China is Mexico's Baluarte Bridge, at 390 meters. Which one would you dare to cross, and what should we rank next?
